title: Mets poised to give top pitching prospect Jonah Tong another start
content:
The New York Mets are strongly considering giving Jonah Tong, their top pitching prospect, another shot in the major leagues soon after the right-hander showed improvement in recent outings.

Tong is scheduled to pitch for Triple-A Syracuse on Saturday, but people familiar with the situation said he is more likely to start for the Mets early next week in their series against the Miami Marlins. The league sources spoke on the condition of anonymity because the club had not yet firmed up its plans. The Mets are set to visit Miami for a three-game series starting on Monday.

Ahead of the Mets’ game Wednesday against the Tampa Bay Rays, Mets interim manager Andy Green told reporters that Tong was “definitely under discussion” as a near-term possibility. The Mets are off on Thursday. The order of their rotation for their weekend series lines up as Nolan McLean, Zac Thornton and Christian Scott.

One of the most important tasks on the Mets’ to-do list over the final few weeks of the season is figuring out which pitchers can help them next season — even if it’s only in a depth capacity. Tong holds enough talent to become an impact starter. His up-and-down season in Triple A, however, cost him opportunities earlier to showcase his capabilities for the Mets’ future.

With the Mets wanting to ease up on Scott’s workload, it makes sense for them to add another starter to the mix for the final few turns. Scott, in his first season back from Tommy John surgery, has logged 20 starts and 94 1/3 innings. While he has a 3.80 ERA for the season, he had a 6.04 ERA in August (five starts). Green said this week that Scott would no longer pitch this season on four days’ rest.

Tong, who debuted in 2025, last pitched in the majors on June 2. In three appearances (10 innings) with the Mets this season, Tong has allowed four earned runs, eight hits and seven walks with seven strikeouts. In five major-league starts last year, Tong had a 7.71 ERA.

Heading into the season, the Mets were counting on Tong as part of their rotation depth. But he experienced a rough season in Triple A while working on different things. His arm angle changed and he tried to emphasize his breaking ball more. Across 23 starts with Syracuse, Tong has a 4.54 ERA.

Now, things are again starting to trend upward for Tong, who led the minor leagues last year in strikeouts (179 in 113 2/3 innings).

Over Tong’s last three starts, he posted a 0.52 ERA with 17 strikeouts and six walks (17 1/3 innings). Last week, he carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning before allowing a single. In recent starts, Tong has pitched more aggressively, attacking hitters with more pitches in the strike zone while also mixing up his repertoire better. In particular, his fastball-changeup combination has stymied batters.
